newsitem.title: USA: Fruit of the Loom to sell hosiery business.
newsitem.headline: Fruit of the Loom to sell hosiery business.

text.p: Fruit of the Loom Inc said Thursday it agreed to sell a substantial portion of its hosiery manufacturing operations to Renfro Corp.
Renfro is a privately held, Mount Airy, N.C.-based company that makes socks sold to leading retailers.
Fruit of the Loom said it expected about $95 million in proceeds from the deal, including working capital items.
In addition, Fruit of the Loom agreed to grant Renfro an exclusive license to use the Fruit of the Loom trade name and trademark on athletic, casual and dress socks for adults and children.
The proposed transaction requires a definitive purchase agreement and approval by directors of both companies.
Fruit of the Loom's plants are located in Starr, N.C., Whitmire, S.C., and DeKalb, Ala. They employ about 1,300 workers.
Employees at the plants are expected to join Renfro.

The company might use proceeds from the sale to retire bank debt, said Mark Steinkrauss, vice president for corporate relations. It was also considering using some of the funds to repurchase shares, he said in a telephone interview.
The company has about 76.1 million shares outstanding.
Fruit of the Loom currently has about $1.4 billion in debt of which about 55 percent is bank debt, he said.
Shares of Fruit of the Loom were trading up 1-1/2 to 31-3/4 at 1310 EDT/1710 GMT.
